title: eval-harness: add prompt-set regression CI hook and quality gating
author: Maya Singh
description: Motivation: CI was not running prompt-set regression checks as a gating step for PRs that touch the model-serving prompts or evaluation harness. This PR adds a lightweight CI hook that runs the canonical prompt regression suite and enforces a quality gate based on configurable thresholds. Summary: - Adds a new CI job `eval-prompt-regression` that runs prompt-set based regressions in a fast, sampled mode for PRs touching eval or prompts. - Introduces a quality gate config file (`ci/eval-gates.yaml`) with thresholds for metric drift, failure rate, and median latency regression. - Implements a reusable hook (eval-harness/ci/hooks/prompt_regression.py) that loads the gate, runs the eval harness in sampled mode, and posts results back to the PR as a status check. - Integrates the hook into the existing GitHub Actions pipeline and the internal CI orchestration (terraform/ci-pipeline.tf). Testing and rollout: - Local unit tests for the hook and a small integration test that mocks model responses are included. - CI runs initially in non-blocking mode for two weeks (flagged via `ci/eval-gates.yaml`) to collect baseline metrics. - After monitoring, the job will be flipped to blocking for PRs that touch `eval-harness/**` or `prompts/**`. Backwards compatibility: the job is opt-in by file globs and defaults to non-blocking so there is no immediate disruption. Checklist: - [x] Add CI job and hook - [x] Add quality gate schema and defaults - [x] Add unit/integration tests - [x] Add PR comment/status reporting - [x] Docs: short guide in docs/eval/quality-gates.md Related: ENG-4620 (follow-up to allow canary thresholds per-team), SUP-1123 (support ticket that motivated stricter prompt regression checks).
